liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The transition from Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain is called phenomenal; The Scarlet into Fire is called one of the sweetest of the eighties, thanks to Mickey and Billy's drumming [14][20]
- **Other One** (1 review): The Space into The Other One sequence is described as trippy [12]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Jerry's playing on They Love Each Other is singled out as outstanding [13]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Bob plays an unusual sliding guitar sound in Not Fade Away, audibly moving along the neck [15]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Played in a light drizzle; raindrops on the pavilion roof can be heard, especially during Weir's breakdown [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd82-08-08 t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t02 Alabama Getaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t03 Promised Land**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t04 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t05 Mama Tried**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t06 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t07 Loser**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd82-08-08 t08 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-08-08.141498.sbd.pcm.healy.streeter.lubar.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 174 min [1]
- **gd1982-08-08.144731.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 23 songs; 179 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: The Other One space is included in this version, with pitch verified by Joe B. Jones [5]
- **gd1982-08-08.167917.senn421.michael.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 23 songs; 175 min [7]. Said about its sound: A short patch in Drums comes from the Dan Healy soundboard source [7]
- **gd82-08-08.sbd.skankweed.15580.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [10]. Said about its sound: This seed has Peggy-O repaired, but Loser is still cut and incomplete [14]
- **gd82-08-08.sbd-wise.unknown.7690.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.05/5 by 20 [11]. Said about its sound: Sound is good, but Phil is a little light in the mix; Reviewer hears several musical, vocal and audio flubs and finds it an off night; Jerry sounds remarkably strong, both vocally and on guitar, by eighties standards [15][19][22]

## Around the show

- Zakir Hussain plays drums with the band from Drums through the end of the show [16]
- John Cipollina sits in on guitar from Not Fade Away to the end [16]
- Zakir Hussain joins the band for Drums [1]
- John Cippolina plays from The Other One through Brokedown Palace [1]
- Reviewer calls this arguably the best Satisfaction the band ever played, though the show may not be top ten [12]
- Reviewer rates the whole run, beginning 7/31, as spectacular [13]
- Reviewer names 6/26/82 and 6/16/82 (Music Mountain) as other notable Jerry shows that summer [14]
- Reviewer claims this is the best Satisfaction the Grateful Dead ever performed [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-08-08.141498.sbd.pcm.healy.streeter.lubar.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Frank Streeter and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Harvey Lubar; source: Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony… [1]
- **gd1982-08-08.144731.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Dan Healy & Frank Streeter; transferred by Matt Smitt, Scott Clugston, Charlier Miller; source: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony TC770/Maxell… [5]. Also: A Beyer M160 front-of-board source supplies crowd sound, the start of Loser, and patches in Estimated Prophet and the Wharf Rat transition [5]
- **gd1982-08-08.167917.senn421.michael.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Rodney Michael; transferred by Tim McKenzie;Charlie Miller;Scott Clugston; source: Rodney Michael's Master FOB (24th row) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M > DAT (x0) > Tim McKenzie's CDR's [7]. Also: Kyle Holbrook's Nakamichi 300 blend patches Mama Tried, the start of Loser, Space, and the last part of Brokedown Palace [7]
- **gd82-08-08.sbd.skankweed.15580.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [10]
- **gd82-08-08.sbd-wise.unknown.7690.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Soundboard [11]
